sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Off-Price Wholesale Liquidation of Branded Overstock Apparel

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Federal State; Aktiengesellschaft registered in the cantonal Commercial Register of its registered seat, e.g., Zug, Geneva or Zurich)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified, Germanic tradition; Swiss Civil Code SR 210 and Code of Obligations SR 220; reinforced by regulatory circulars of FINMA, SECO and the Federal Commercial Register Office)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BIT Switzerland - People's Republic of China (1986; revised protocol in force 2010)
DTA Switzerland - People's Republic of China (2013; amended protocol in force 2018)
DTA Switzerland - United States of America (1996; amended protocol in force 2019)
EFTA Convention (Vaduz Convention, in force 1 June 2002) and EFTA free trade agreements with non-EU states (e.g., Singapore, Canada, South Korea)
Trade Agreement Switzerland - United Kingdom (in force 1 January 2021)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Articles 620-663b on the Aktiengesellschaft (stock corporation); incorporation requirements Articles 626-633, minimum capital Article 632, capital deposit confirmation Article 634, commercial register entry Article 640, registration application Article 643; supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411) and the Swiss Civil Code (SR 210) on legal personality.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug); final supervisory authority is the Federal Commercial Register Office within the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister (Application for Entry into the Commercial Register), consisting of the notarised public deed of incorporation and the company's Articles of Incorporation (Statuten).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (Article 632 OR). At least 20% of the nominal value of each share, in aggregate no less than CHF 50,000, must be paid up in cash before filing; the funds are held in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank and released only upon Commercial Register entry. A bank confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) must accompany the application; any contribution in kind requires a review report by a licensed audit firm.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
This First Board Resolution of [Company Name] AG is adopted at the constituent board meeting held at the registered office in Zug on [date].

1. Share Subscription: Each founder subscribes to the registered share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value, paid up per Article 7 of the Articles of Incorporation.

2. Registered Office: The board designates [street address], Zug, Switzerland as the statutory registered office, effective upon Commercial Register entry.

3. Officer Appointments: The board appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Secretary, with signatory authority per the signature regulation.

4. Authorisation: The board authorises the Chairperson to complete the Commercial Register filing and open the company's bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil-Law Notarisation of Articles of Incorporation and Founder Signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public for the Canton of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear before a Zug notary together with passports and the finalised Statuten. The public deed must state the company name ending in AG/SA, corporate purpose (wholesale trading and off-price liquidation of finished garments and branded overstock apparel), registered office in Zug, share capital, share classes, board composition, auditor, and system of representation. The notary verifies the absence of a sectoral licence requirement, authenticates the signatures, and issues the public instrument required for the registry filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each founder
Final draft Articles of Incorporation (Statuten)
Written declaration of no disqualifying criminal record
Draft share register (Aktienbuch)
List of founders with exact share allocations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal deficiencies, the deed is amended and re-certified; the only consequence is additional notarial fees and a re-run of the notary appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-Up Capital in Blocked Escrow Account and Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank - Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS Switzerland AG, Escrow Account Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators open a blocked corporate escrow account (Sperrkonto) in the company's formation name and deposit no less than CHF 50,000 (or the full CHF 100,000 if so decided). Each beneficial owner is identified under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act; the bank issues a Liberierungsbestätigung certifying account holder, deposit amount, and the blocking instruction valid until Commercial Register entry.
required_dossiers: Company formation name and corporate purpose
Passports of signatories and beneficial-owner declaration
Evidence of the source of funds
Bank KYC/AML forms
Draft or notarised Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines onboarding, the applicant approaches an alternative licensed Swiss bank; there is no statutory right to a specific bank, and disputes are handled through the Swiss Banking Ombudsman as a non-binding channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Processing of the Commercial Register Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Chairperson of the Board submits the electronic Application for Entry via the Swiss Commercial Register telematics portal (Handelsregister-Telematik) attaching all notarised and certified documents. The registry legally screens the name, purpose, capital and signatory powers; on approval the company is entered, the entry is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), and the company acquires legal personality retroactively to the deed date.
required_dossiers: Notarised public deed of incorporation
Articles of Incorporation (Statuten)
Bank confirmation Liberierungsbestätigung
Board member acceptance declarations and certified signature specimens
Criminal record excerpts of directors, where requested
Founder list and share allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A requisition (Vormerkung) is cured by filing supplementary declarations within the set deadline; a negative decision is appealable to the Zug Cantonal Administrative Court and then to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court under Article 940 OR in conjunction with Article 156 HRegV.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Automatic UID Issuance and OASI Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) - UID Register; Compensation Office of the Canton of Zug (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register automatically transmits incorporation data to the central business identification register, which issues the UID number. The compensation office establishes the employer number under AHV/IV/EO, registers the company for family allowances (FAK), and the employer contractually joins a BVG occupational pension foundation and SUVA or a private accident insurer for statutory accident coverage of employees.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug)
Employer registration form (Arbeitgeber-Anmeldung)
Employees' AHV numbers and employment contracts
BVG pension foundation confirmation
SUVA or private accident insurance confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Corrections to UID or OASI data are processed through the compensation office self-service portal; late registration is strictly cured retroactively, but administrative fines can be avoided by filing within 30 days of the Commercial Register entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal VAT Registration and Cantonal Tax File Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Main Division, Bern; Cantonal Tax Office of Zug (Steuerverwaltung des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company files the electronic VAT registration (formular 754) on the ESTV portal declaring projected taxable turnover, place of supply and any drop-shipping logistics. Under the revised Swiss VAT Act, registration is mandatory when annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, with the threshold rising to CHF 250,000 effective 1 January 2025; an active apparel wholesaler registers unless a genuine exemption applies. Simultaneously, the cantonal tax file for corporate income and equity tax is opened with the Zug tax authority.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
UID number
Forecast of taxable supplies in Switzerland and abroad
Warehouse and third-party logistics description
Board resolution appointing the VAT compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ESTV questions the turnover forecast or threshold, the company submits revised projections and underlying purchase orders; assessment disputes follow the 30-day appeal to the ESTV and onward appeal to the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operating Bank Account Activation and Municipal Premises Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of the company (e.g. UBS Switzerland AG or Zuger Kantonalbank); Municipality of Zug, Building and Economic Affairs Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The bank receives the final Commercial Register excerpt and the board resolution on signatory authority; it activates the Swiss franc current account and the USD and EUR accounts supporting Swift Wire and ACH Direct payment rails. The municipality is notified of the warehouse and office trade premises for zoning consistency, fire-safety classification and waste-collection planning; any change of use in the building requires a municipal usage-change permit.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register excerpt no older than 30 days
Board resolution on bank signatories
Identity papers of persons with disposal authority
Municipal premises notification and warehouse floor plan
Fire-safety certificate for the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Zoning inconsistencies are remedied by applying for an administrative exception (Ausnahmebewilligung) under the Zug Planning and Building Act; refusal may be appealed to the cantonal building authority within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Switzerland imposes no sectoral industrial licence on ISIC 4641 wholesale apparel liquidation; the only authorities with standing are the Commercial Register Office (registration) and the Municipality of Zug (premises and fire safety).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence is statutorily required; the Commercial Register entry (Eintragung) itself confers the trading authorisation, and the Canton of Zug does not issue a trade certificate (Gewerbeschein) for pure wholesale off-price garment trading.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU); Cantonal Environment Office of Zug (Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - warehousing and wholesale distribution of finished garments is not listed in Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV, SR 814.011), so no full EIA report or preliminary scoping is required unless the specific building thresholds of the UVPV Annex (category building projects) are exceeded by the chosen warehouse site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: sanitary discharges only, connected to the public sewer under the Water Protection Act (SR 814.20) and Water Protection Ordinance (SR 814.201) with municipal discharge limits; emissions: negligible VOC load since no dyeing, printing or coating is performed, with the precautionary principle of the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) applying; waste: unsold, returned and off-specification garments must be sorted, documented and disposed of through licensed facilities under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600), while textiles destined for reuse or export are classified as goods and freely shipped under World Trade Organization rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification of the warehouse and office premises under the Swiss fire protection standard (VKF/AEAI) issued by the Building Insurance of Zug; structural load inspection certificate for pallet racking issued by the municipal building inspectorate; occupational safety clearance from SUVA and the Federal Coordination Commission for Occupational Safety (EKAS) covering manual handling of garment bales, forklift traffic, emergency escape plans, first-aid equipment and statutory accident insurance cover.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), VAT and Special Taxes Division; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT registration and filing portal: S-VAT (system-tva.swiss / vat-form.estv.admin.ch); UID registry: www.uid.admin.ch. Cantonal and communal tax administrations administer direct taxes at their respective levels.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity conducting taxable activities in Switzerland must register for Swiss VAT via the S-VAT portal using the official VAT registration form, either immediately upon commencing activities or at the moment it exceeds the statutory CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover threshold (Art. 63 VAT Act). The FTA then assigns the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / identification d'entreprise IDE) and the MWST/TVA VAT registration number. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft must additionally obtain a UID through the cantonal commercial register (Handelsregisteramt) before or upon incorporation; the UID serves as the sole statutory business tax and VAT identification number for all tax authorities. Non-resident entities may nominate a Swiss tax representative for VAT compliance when they have no domestic seat or establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Swiss resident companies (AG) are subject to federal corporate income tax at the statutory rate of 8.5% (effective approximately 15–21% including cantonal and communal profit taxes depending on canton). Territorial scope: worldwide income for tax residents, with unilateral relief exempting foreign permanent establishment profits and real estate (bracket system) and a participation exemption for dividends and capital gains from qualifying substantial shareholdings; the STAF 2020 framework abolished privileged tax statuses (holding, mixed, principal company) and replaced them with broadly applicable instruments (patent box, R&D super-deduction, notional interest deduction). No general tax-exempt zones exist for the wholesale apparel trading sector; ordinary domestic tax rates apply throughout Switzerland.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or analogous entity classification election exists under Swiss law. Available elections: (1) VAT group taxation election (Art. 20 VAT Act) combining economically integrated enterprises into a single taxable person; (2) election of the partial taxation method or the effective input VAT apportionment method for mixed-use activities; (3) under the STAF 2020 rules, election of the patent box regime or the R&D additional deduction for qualifying income; (4) for distributions from qualifying participations, election of the 'partial taxation method' at cantonal level; (5) Swiss anti-hybrid mismatch rules (effective 1 January 2020) apply IPIC/ATAD2-style deduction/no-inclusion disallowances; no elective opt-out is available for hybrid entities, but structured transactions are assessed for tax treaty and substance override.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (SR 641.20; VAT Act / MWSTG / LTVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10 VAT Act) for entrepreneurs with their seat or place of business in Switzerland; foreign entities supplying services from abroad or digital B2C services register when the CHF 100,000 threshold from Swiss-source supplies is reached (Art. 11 para. 1 VAT Act). Low-value import consignments below CHF 65 import value are exempt from import VAT; no simplified small-business scheme is available once turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, except for charities, sport event organisers and non-profit entities with separate thresholds (e.g., CHF 150,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not apply a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, government API stamping, or digital stamping regime for B2B or B2C invoices. The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is the standardised electronic invoice format, and eBill is offered by retail banks. A Federal Council reform announced in 2024 envisages mandatory B2B domestic e-invoicing with a phased introduction from 2028; implementing legislation is pending. Until then, VAT deduction is substantiated by conventional invoices that meet Art. 26 VAT Act content requirements; no government pre-clearance or electronic signature mandate applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated (tax-exempt with entitlement to input VAT deduction) under Art. 23 para. 1 VAT Act when the exporter proves that the goods were actually transported or dispatched abroad and the recipient is outside Switzerland (or the goods are placed into a customs warehouse). Goods must leave Switzerland in an unaltered state or after minor processing supported by a valid outward customs declaration. Services qualify as zero-rated export services (Art. 23 para. 2 VAT Act) where the recipient is located abroad or the service relates to movable tangible property exported from Switzerland, provided the service is demonstrably rendered for foreign use. Full documentary evidence of export and of the recipient's foreign residence/seat is mandatory for the 0% rate to apply; the burden of proof lies on the exporter in all cases.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Outward customs export declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration / déclaration d'exportation) processed via the Swiss customs clearance system (e-dec or ESA)
Commercial invoice (sales invoice for off-price garments) issued to the foreign buyer and conforming to Art. 26 VAT Act invoice content requirements
Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or CMR road consignment note evidencing actual cross-border transport
Proof of receipt/payment of export consideration (SWIFT bank statement or inward remittance confirmation) demonstrating the foreign-linked commercial flow
Period-end export register and, where applicable, warehouse movement records (for customs warehouses or third-country transit)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA audits zero-rated export claims primarily via desk reviews of customs and payment evidence; any non-documented or fraudulent zero-rating is retroactively clawed back by means of VAT re-assessment (Nachbelastung) plus default interest at 4.5% per annum. Willful or grossly negligent export VAT evasion constitutes tax evasion under Art. 56 VAT Act, for which the FTA may impose a penalty of up to three times the VAT evaded (or one time where negligence is committed), in addition to criminal fines of up to CHF 100,000; simple procedural infractions carry fines up to CHF 10,000. The limitation period for VAT enforcement is generally five years from the end of the relevant fiscal period, extended to ten years in cases of deliberate evasion, and the FTA retains the right to require security or arrange company-level VAT rulings for repeated offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banca Nazionale Svizzera / Banca Naziunala Svizra), with settlement infrastructure operated by SIX Interbank Clearing Ltd via SIC and EuroSIC
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully liberalised current and capital account; the Swiss franc is freely convertible for residents and non-residents, and there are no exchange-control restrictions under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA) or the National Bank Act. Profit remittance, debt service, liquidation proceeds and trade payments may flow abroad without prior SNB authorisation. The only structural hurdle to outbound distributions is the 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividend payments, which is refundable or treaty-reduced under applicable double-taxation agreements, and the absence of capital controls does not relieve the collecting Swiss bank from its statutory AML/CFT documentation duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters of off-price garments may retain proceeds in CHF or any freely convertible foreign currency in resident or non-resident accounts, and the SNB requires no repatriation declaration other than statistical balance-of-payments reporting by the Swiss bank for individual cross-border payments exceeding CHF 10 million within a calendar year.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) and Operational Settlement Account (Betriebskonto) with trade-finance desk
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Trades Account covering documentary credit issuance
Operational Treasury Account for CHF and EUR invoice settlements
Operational Settlement Account with SIC5 instant-payment access

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. FINMA-licensed fintech entities holding a banking licence or a FinTech licence under Art. 1b of the Banking Act may hold client deposits up to CHF 100 million and access SIC rails; however, foreign EMIs authorised in the EU or UK cannot passport into Switzerland because Switzerland is neither an EEA member nor an equivalently recognised payments jurisdiction, and a non-Swiss EMI without a FINMA branch licence cannot open a settlement account at SIX and may only reach CHF payments through a Swiss correspondent banking partner, materially weakening treasury control for the off-price wholesale flow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory physical appearance is not mandated by the Swiss Code of Obligations, but Swiss banking practice requires at least the ultimate beneficial owner and one authorised signatory to complete an onboarding interview, either in person at the bank's Swiss premises or remotely by video verified against the passport and a notarised signature certificate (Unterschriftsbeglaubigung); remote opening is accepted by selected cantonal banks and FinTechs on a risk-weighted basis for a Low_Risk_Standard apparel wholesaler, while banks retain full discretion to refuse purely digital identification for non-resident board members.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain hiding the natural-person owner through a Hong Kong or Panama intermediate company while the Swiss AG acts as liquidity pass-through.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited ownership cascade from the Swiss Commercial Register extract; the final UBO's passport with apostille; a board resolution confirming the UBO structure under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and AMLO-FINMA; and audited or reviewed financial statements of the intermediate entity evidencing a genuine trading purpose rather than conduit status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity inconsistent with declared turnover, e.g., repeated large incoming wires from foreign discount-retail chains without supporting documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-consignment trade file containing signed purchase contracts, supplier purchase orders, mobile bills of lading, Swiss customs declarations, the vendor's off-price certificate showing the liquidation discount formula, and an aged receivable reconciliation matching each SWIFT credit to its invoice reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to third-party freight forwarders or factoring agents at the direction of foreign customers, creating an indirect beneficiary pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tripartite written agreement among the Swiss AG, the customer, and the logistics provider expressly authorising the disbursement; contract references embedded in MT103 field 70; a due-diligence file on the freight forwarder prepared in line with AMLO-FINMA; and a legal opinion confirming that the payment does not constitute a disguised transfer of customer funds under Swiss debt-collection or money-laundering norms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Directors inject the AG's capital through a SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with SIC settlement into a reserved Capital Escrow Account; the remittance information carries the balance-of-payments purpose classification of a direct-investment equity contribution, and the Swiss bank issues a capital-payment confirmation (Einzahlungsbestätigung) evidencing the paid-up portion of the statutory minimum CHF 100,000 nominal share capital under Articles 626 to 632 of the Swiss Code of Obligations. Cross-border credits exceeding CHF 10 million per bank per year trigger only statistical SNB reporting and require no prior regulatory approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for liquidation stock purchases run primarily over SWIFT MT103 with SIC for CHF and EuroSIC for EUR clearing; larger or higher-risk consignments are secured through irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700 and, where needed, standby letters of credit under ISP98 via MT760. Each outbound credit must carry the contract and invoice reference in the remittance field to survive the correspondent bank's sanctions and AML screening; ACH-Direct and SIC5 instant payment are acceptable only for small, fully-verified counterparties below the bank's pre-set threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla CHF/EUR and CHF/USD outright forward contracts with Swiss banking counterparties under the Swiss Master Agreement for OTC derivatives
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps under ISDA 2002 or the Swiss Master Agreement, with margin collateral requirements applying under FINMA rules for non-centrally cleared derivatives
Vanilla FX call and put options traded under ISDA 2002 for hedging the EUR and USD receivable book

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the counterparty jurisdiction imposes convertibility or delivery restrictions preventing CHF settlement; domestically NDFs are operationally de-prioritised because CHF is freely deliverable
Exchange-traded FX futures listed on EU or US venues remain legally usable but are rarely adopted by a mid-sized AG due to margin and operational friction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return with annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date for calendar-year AG, generally by 30 June; extensions available on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, default assessment, administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; enforced debt collection may trigger liquidation but not direct commercial-register strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the quarterly, semi-annual, or annual VAT period assigned by ESTV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder fee, default interest at 5% p.a., default tax assessment, penalty up to CHF 8,000 for omission; enforced recovery may lead to bankruptcy but not automatic strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/IV/EO employer wage declaration and contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage declaration by 31 January following the calendar year; contribution payments due in accordance with AHV payment plan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a., administrative surcharge, fines for employers failing to deduct employee social contributions; no direct commercial-register strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss statutory audit report, where ordinary or limited audit applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General meeting of shareholders; submitted to tax authorities as annex to the corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report must be available before the AGM, which must be held within 6 months after balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Profit appropriation may be contested, tax assessment may be reopened, and director/auditor liability may arise; no automatic commercial-register strike-off for audit deficiency alone

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary (mandatory) audit is required if a Swiss AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: CHF 20 million total assets, CHF 40 million net turnover, and 250 average annual full-time employees; companies with listed equity or public bonds are always subject to ordinary audit. A limited audit applies when shareholders representing at least 10% of the share capital so request and the company is not subject to ordinary audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) annual accounts as the legal base; Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS permitted as supplementary or consolidated framework; IFRS/Swiss GAAP FER effectively required for listed group undertakings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not currently impose an annual central UBO confirmation filing for a privately held Aktiengesellschaft. The company must maintain an up-to-date share register recording owners of registered shares; on each share transfer, the acquiring person or entity is entered upon proof of acquisition. Financial intermediaries must verify and retain beneficial-owner data before entering into business relationships, but no annual public UBO return is filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Responsible Persons
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 3,500 per year in a typical Zurich, Geneva, or Zug fiduciary/registered-office service arrangement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 18,000 for a statutory ordinary audit; USD 2,500 – 6,500 for a limited audit or review engagement where eligible

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal corporate income tax levied on post-tax profit (equivalent to approx. 7.83% on a pre-tax basis); combined federal, cantonal and communal effective rate for a Zug AG approximates 11.9% for the 2025 assessment period.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: STAF-derived reliefs: mandatory tax patent box (up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP income), additional deductions for qualifying R&D (150% effective deduction), notional interest deduction on excess equity, and participation relief (95% dividend exemption on shareholdings above 10% and CHF 1 million), plus cantonal multipliers in Zug set at a competitive low level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration d'impôt des personnes morales) covering federal direct tax (DBG), cantonal and communal tax (StG/ZUG); filed electronically via the cantonal tax administration e-filing system (canton Zug portal) with a single annual declaration for all three levies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must generally be filed by 31 March of the subsequent year; canton Zug normally grants an automatic extension to 30 September, with additional extension available on reasoned request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: AG legal name, UID number, Swiss Tax Identification Number, commercial register seat, fiscal status, board members, principal business activity (ISIC 4641 apparel wholesale and liquidation trading).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and directors must indicate country of residence, tax identification number and bank jurisdiction; no nominee or bearer-shareholder arrangements may be declared without full beneficial-owner disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory annual accounts as filed with the commercial register, showing assets, liabilities, equity, inventory valuation of off-price finished garments, receivables, intercompany payables and bank balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany balances with foreign related parties must reconcile with complete local file documentation; non-resident shareholder loans must be at arm's length and are subject to Swiss thin-capitalisation safe harbour debt/equity thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit before tax, operating income from wholesale liquidation sales, gross margin, operating expenses, depreciation, freight and logistics costs, and bad debt provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border management, marketing and sourcing fees paid to related foreign entities must be evidenced by written agreements, actual services and mark-ups consistent with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from commercial profit to taxable profit: add-back of non-deductible expenses, reduction for participation relief, patent box deduction, notional interest deduction, and deduction of prior-year loss carryforwards (7-year limit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled entities must disclose all related-party adjustments; undocumented foreign tax credits or hidden profit distributions to foreign shareholders will be recharacterised as deemed dividends subject to Swiss withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Dividend distribution and withholding tax declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of proposed or actual gross dividends, liquidation proceeds and similar distributions subject to Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent AG must claim treaty relief via Form 105 refund application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA), supported by a current Residence Certificate of tax residence; the Swiss company must file and remit the 35% anticipatory tax on the gross distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Procedural late-filing fines (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 1,500 per infringement; default interest on assessed corporate income tax (currently approx. 4.5% p.a.); intentional or negligent misdeclaration triggers Steuerhinterziehung penalties of one to three times the evaded tax, and repeated or fraudulent misconduct triggers criminal prosecution with imprisonment for responsible organs.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends distributed by a Swiss AG; fully refundable or reduced under applicable double taxation agreements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The paying Swiss AG must deduct and remit 35%; the non-resident beneficial owner submits Form 105 to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration together with a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and proof of beneficial ownership to claim the excess above the DTA rate; typical DTA rates are 5% on substantial shareholdings and 15% on portfolio dividends, with refunds processed only after the tax has been remitted to the FTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: interest on Swiss bond issues and deposit-bearing bank accounts is subject to 35% anticipatory tax; ordinary intercompany debt interest is not subject to Swiss withholding tax of a statutory character; royalties for intellectual property have 0% Swiss statutory withholding tax. Under most Swiss DTAs, interest and royalties are exempt (0%) at source, while dividend withholding is capped at 5-15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full OECD-aligned Local File and Master File documentation is expected where a Swiss taxpayer's aggregate annual intragroup transactions exceed CHF 10 million across any category (goods, services, financing, intangibles); below that threshold, a simplified short-form ('Kurzbericht') documentation is accepted. Switzerland imposes no separate statutory TP return, but the FTA and cantons may formally order documentation under the federal assessment procedure and apply penalties for non-production.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply the offshore Economic Substance Regulations model; however, the risk-based substance doctrine operates through the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test (PPT), the Swiss general anti-abuse clause and administrative practice requiring physical presence, qualified personnel, active decision-making, real inventory movement and commercial premises in Switzerland. A garment liquidation trading AG lacking genuine substance in Zug would be denied tax treaty benefits, exposed to look-through taxation of the foreign shareholders, and reclassified as a shell company, with retroactive assessment and criminal implications.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submission of tax returns with under-declared profits, concealed overstock inventory, fictitious cost deductions, hidden Swiss bank accounts, or unrecorded cash sales in the off-price wholesale operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of one to three times the evaded federal tax (Art. 175 DBG); cantonal recoupment interest at statutory rate; loss of appeal rights; publication of the final penalty decision; reinstatement of assessments for ten years in cases of intentional omission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director, CFO or head of finance is subject to personal criminal fines and, in aggravated or repeated cases, criminal conviction with imprisonment up to three years; corporate res judicata does not extinguish individual culpability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of falsified invoices, backdated purchase contracts, forged customs documents, fabricated intercompany invoices for liquidation stock, or computer manipulation of accounting records to deceive the tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment up to five years and a monetary fine under the Swiss Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law (VStrG); directly assessed fraudulent profit tax; unlimited limitation period for false accounting instruments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and others signatory to fraudulent records face personal criminal prosecution, travel restrictions and bank account freezes; courts may impose unlimited personal liability for the resulting tax damage upon proof of willful participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Deduct and Remit Anticipatory Tax (Verrechnungssteuer)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, deemed dividends or liquidation proceeds to the foreign shareholder without deducting and remitting the 35% statutory withholding tax, including hidden profit distributions through non-arm's length intercompany prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Statutory payment claim for the full 35% of the gross distribution plus statutory default interest; administrative penalty of up to the amount of tax evaded; blockage of any treaty refund claim for the period of the violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable without a prior benefit requirement to the FTA for unremitted anticipatory tax; deliberate omission constitutes criminal fiscal misconduct with personal fines and potential custodial sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a registered office and tax residence in Zug while actual purchasing, warehousing, logistics, invoicing and decision-making occur abroad; using the off-price garment wholesale model solely to channel commissions or liquidation profits to a disregarded foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the PPT anti-abuse rule; reclassification of the AG as economically transparent; addition of profit at the Swiss level as hidden profit distributions; withdrawal of cooperative tax ruling; retroactive tax assessments and negligence penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who operate the letterbox entity expose themselves to civil restructuring and bankruptcy liability with potential personal restitution of misallocated profits, entry into the commercial register exclusion procedure, and travel bans in the context of tax execution proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering (AML) Deficiency in Cash Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting substantial cash settlements for liquidation pallets, receiving customer funds through undisclosed third-party accounts, or deliberately avoiding the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act threshold applicable to goods traders (cash transactions above CHF 100,000), despite the Low_Risk_Standard tier of the underlying apparel wholesale business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty against the company of up to CHF 500,000 for violation of due diligence, identification and reporting duties; forfeiture of laundered assets; suspension of the entity from public procurement and payment settlement infrastructure; additional supervisory enforcement orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and compliance officers are personally liable for breaches of AML due diligence duties; where intent or criminal negligence is proven, personal criminal conviction with imprisonment up to five years, personal fines, disqualification from serving as directors, and civil liability for all consequential tax losses sustained by the estate.
